subject: EOQ reflections, playbook, and risk register
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-25T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: EOQ reflections, playbook, and risk register

Team —

Attached is a short pack (EOQ_playbook_v1.pdf) that consolidates our end-of-quarter OKR scoring rationale, a one-page playbook for the QBR meeting with Acme Analytics, and a risk register highlighting open evidence gaps for their security review. High level:

- Proposed public-facing QBR slides (QBR_slide_draft.pptx) that focus on latency/cost improvements and the new routing policy experiments.
- Recommended OKR adjustments (section 2) — I flagged three items where scores should move from 75% -> 60% based on customer-impact evidence.
- Risk register includes the SOC2 evidence gaps Acme asked for; Monica and Laura, I put the requested artifacts into score_evidence_ACM-4892.csv.

Asks:
1) Please review the scoring notes (page 6) and call out any disagreements in-line by EOD Pacific today.
2) If you approve the QBR slide direction, I’ll lock and share with Samira at Acme for preread by tomorrow afternoon.
3) Monica, can you confirm the security evidence items we still need and ETA?

I included a short suggested script for the QBR (last page) — keeps the exec narrative tight and puts the product improvements in cost/latency terms.

[Attachment: EOQ_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]
[Attachment: QBR_slide_draft.pptx (PPTX, 2.4MB)]
[Attachment: score_evidence_ACM-4892.csv (CSV, 32KB)]

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success & Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-25T09:09:00-08:00
Subject: Re: EOQ reflections, playbook, and risk register

Ben — quick read through; two quick notes:

- I agree with tightening the public narrative to cost/latency gains. Small ask: add one slide with a clear before/after for the KV cache rollout (ops numbers). Customers always love that.
- On scores: I’m okay moving Product Reliability to 60% given the two incident regressions this quarter, but we should capture the mitigation plan in the slide notes.

Will leave further scoring comments inline in the drive doc.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — I pulled the SOC2/Documents checklist into the security tracker and annotated expected delivery dates. Summary:

- Evidence ready today: encryption-at-rest policy, KMS rotation proof, audit-log sample (attached as references in the CSV).
- Evidence pending: HSM key attestation (vendor delay) — estimated delivery 2027-03-04.
- Short-term mitigation: we can provide a signed attestation from our infra partner and a temporary SOC2 self-attestation for the QBR; customer has accepted that previously for time-boxed reviews, but we should flag as a risk.

For scoring: I recommend we move two sub-metrics under Security from 80 -> 65 because of the HSM attestation delay. I added the line items in score_evidence_ACM-4892.csv.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-25T13:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: EOQ reflections, playbook, and risk register

All — thanks for the quick turn. A few decisions to lock before we share externally: 

1) OKR scores: Approve the proposed adjustments (Product Reliability -> 60%; Security sub-metrics -> 65%). Putting the lowered scores in the QBR is honest and gives us room to present an action plan.
2) QBR slides: add Laura’s before/after KV cache slide and a one-line remediation timeline for the reliability incidents.
3) Risk language: Monica, we will not call out the vendor delay by name in the client-facing deck; instead, we’ll say "external attestation pending — mitigation in place" and include a private appendix with the expected delivery date.
4) Owner assignments: Ben, please own the customer preread and timing with Samira. Monica, please upload a redacted audit-log example to the Drive link by EOD.

I’m comfortable with Ben sharing the draft with Acme for preread tomorrow afternoon.

Vivek
CTO (acting)
Redwood Inference

Subject: EOQ reflections, playbook, and risk register — QBR preread (Redwood / Acme)

Samira / Acme team —

Thanks again for your partnership this quarter. For your preread ahead of our QBR next Tuesday, attached are: the EOQ playbook (narrative + scoring rationale), the draft QBR slide deck, and a CSV extract of evidence items requested during the security review. The deck highlights the latency and cost wins from our recent routing optimizations and lays out the near-term reliability mitigations we’ll execute over the next 30 days.

A few notes for context:
- We adjusted a small number of internal OKR scores to reflect incident impacts and an outstanding external attestation; we want to be transparent and pair that with clear remediation timelines (page 5 of the playbook).
- We will keep the technical appendix redacted for the public deck but can provide more detailed evidence under an NDA if you prefer.

Please flag any clarifying questions by EOD tomorrow and we’ll incorporate feedback before the QBR.

Best,
Ben

Director, Customer Success & Sales
Redwood Inference
